words.quote: they are just too boring
the design is a bit boring
Better, but still a bit boring

rows.look_for: Every view has a second layer at 10 m (tones of a field's hue, pinlines, a dissolve, stripe bundles, linework), not only the big shape. No plain field larger than a door on a side, or than the bonnet on top. No view plainer than the brief's favourites, none as plain as the boring anchors.
rows.where: Every shot and its distance image, beside the favourite and boring anchors

words.quote: The back design is nice, but the front is a bit boring
I like the pixel design a lot, but it's totally missing from the front

rows.look_for: The front carries the same system as the sides and tail, as layered: bonnet, bumper, splitter and front fenders, not a plain field or another idea.
rows.where: front34, top (bonnet), nose crop, against rear34

words.quote: it would look a lot better if there where some kind of "stroke" between the colors?

rows.look_for: Where two fields meet, the edge is an event (a pinline, a dissolve, a raked cut) all along it, even in width, and visible in the shots, not lost to thinness or low contrast.
rows.where: side_l, side_r, beltline and nose crops

words.quote: The side text is a bit boring
Here the alignment/spacing on the text is off

rows.look_for: One type system per field: a designation with small lines aligned to it, a shared left edge or baseline, even line gaps, padding and tracking, one display face used decisively. Not a stack of labels.
rows.where: Full side shots, top, every crop with text

words.quote: There's a weird "ai generated/diffusion model" vibe to these
again, a bit AI like

rows.look_for: Letters and marks keep a font's own forms or clean geometry. Fails on soft or melted joins, rounded-off corners, filled counters, or letters that change width or weight from one to the next.
rows.where: Full shots and crops, every wordmark and line of text

words.quote: just remove the wordmark (or keep it smaller/more descrete), it's not imporant for my own personal brand

rows.look_for: The brief decides. Where the brief asks for a lead brand, it reads from the side, from the front (bonnet or nose) and from behind (rear deck or bumper). A brief that asks for none, or for it small, passes when the car follows it.

words.quote: reads as 'YO-3'
reads 'PE-01' under the sim's light panel
a sill sponsor shows as fragments under the side blade

rows.look_for: No text, mark or number is cut, bent or hidden by a wheel arch, the side blade, a crease, a shut line, the sim's light panel or its number. Every word reads whole wherever it shows.
rows.where: Full side shots, front34, rear34, crops

words.quote: Theres a wierd "slant" to the side-line
the black horizontal line is still not perfectly algined
see the differences on the wheel arches

rows.look_for: A line drawn straight runs straight and level: no slant, step or doubling at a seam or shut line, the same height either side of an arch and on both sides. A failure is a kit fault: it goes under `blocked`, for the owner, not into a fix.

words.quote: there are more lines on the bonnet that then texture seems to apply

rows.look_for: No line the design doesn't draw: no light hairlines along seams or panel edges, no base colour showing at a shut line or round lights and vents. A failure is a renderer or kit fault: under `blocked`.

words.quote: The line across the top is a bit to straight compare to the more "natural" curves found elsewhere in the design
The side pod "sponser square" looks very rectangular/boxy when seen directly from the side

rows.look_for: Every element, sponsor plates and fields included, takes the proportions and edges of the design's own shapes. Fails on one element that reads as a bare primitive beside the rest: a ruler-straight run in a design of curves, or a plain hard-edged box where the shapes round it are stretched, stepped or interleaved. A rectangle on a car of rectangles still fails when it is the one plain box.
